judged_text: remove_member performs group.users.delete(user_id) — an immediate, unconditional join-table deletion — and only then uses group.save's result to decide the response, diverging from the previous code path that called group.remove(user). If group.save fails validation after the deletion has already been committed, the API returns an error while the removal has actually taken effect (reported failure over completed work); and the raw association delete bypasses whatever GroupUser destroy-callback maintenance (e.g. user_count bookkeeping) the Group#remove path performed, so the next admin group index render can show a stale user_count.

adjudication.rationale: In `Admin::GroupsController#remove_member`, the code executes `group.users.delete(user_id)` (which immediately deletes the join record) and only afterward uses `group.save` to decide whether to return success or `render_json_error` (diff: `group.users.delete(user_id)` then `if group.save ... else ...`). Since the removal has already been committed, a failing `group.save` would yield an error response even though the member was removed. Also, this bypasses the previous membership-removal path (`group.remove(user)` used elsewhere in the old controller logic), which could skip any removal-specific callbacks/maintenance that method performed; the diff itself confirms the bypass even if the exact callbacks aren’t shown.
